instruction: Create a single-page SVG action scene of a person descending beside a dramatic cliff with an open parachute. Clearly show the cliff edge and rock layers, the suspended human figure, taut harness lines, a fully inflated canopy, wind or motion cues, and distant landscape depth. Compose the scene so the relationship between height, danger, and safe descent is immediately readable. Put strong emphasis on dynamic scale, clear silhouette, atmospheric depth, and polished editorial illustration.

history.critique: Brief & Intent: The required elements are present but the frame fails the brief's core test — 'height, danger, safe descent immediately readable.' The scene is cropped at the viewport fold, so the cliff lip, the full suspended figure, and any drop to a distant valley floor are never seen together; the 'dramatic cliff' is a flat, muddy brown wall whose strata are near-invisible thin lines, and the canopy overlaps the lip, hiding the edge the brief asks to be clearly shown. Distant depth is just two blue-grey bands with no haze gradient or scale references, so altitude and danger are not felt. Clarity & Hierarchy: Focal priority is contested — the bright sun disc and the red canopy both pull the eye, while the human subject (the actual 'person' in the brief) is a tiny dark smudge with a weak silhouette; the taut harness lines are thin and low-contrast against the sky. The right rail duplicates data (4.6 appears in both the DESCENT RATE slider and the TELEMETRY dial) and presents slider/toggle affordances that read as interactive but are static, creating false affordance. The 01–04 annotation callouts are too small to read and their leader lines cross the canopy, adding clutter to the hero object. Visual System & Craft: The cream/clay/slate/sky palette and the serif-display + mono-label type system are coherent and editorial, and the viewfinder corner ticks are a nice touch. But craft breaks down inside the scene: the canopy is a flat red dome with vertical ribs that reads as a mushroom rather than a wind-loaded parachute (no cell structure, no tilt, no leading/trailing light); the figure's pose doesn't read as 'suspended in harness'; the wind streaks are random thin lines that collide with annotation text; an unresolved dark vertical band sits at the scene's left edge like an unfinished vignette; the sun's halo muddies the canopy's right rim; and the bottom of the page clips the NOMINAL status. Expressiveness & Distinctiveness: The 'field study / plate Nº 07' framing, metadata block, and diagrammatic callouts give it a genuinely authored identity rather than template styling — this is the piece's strongest asset. The trade-off is that this diagrammatic richness is currently spent on micro-annotations that don't scale, while the scene itself (red dome + stick figure + flat wall) is generic and lacks the atmospheric drama the identity promises. Real trade-offs: (1) annotation richness vs. scene legibility — the callouts build identity but clutter and are illegible; (2) instrument-panel chrome vs. static SVG deliverable — sliders imply function the brief doesn't require; (3) dark cliff mass vs. dark figure silhouette — the figure needs separation from the rock, but the canopy currently sits on the lip, so fixing one breaks the other; (4) scale drama vs. single-view composition — selling 'dynamic scale' wants a tall drop, but the current crop hides it.
history.suggestion: One prioritized plan, in order: 1) Recompose for the brief's core read — extend/reframe the scene so cliff lip, figure, and a hazy far-below valley floor sit in one view; shift the canopy+figure right and down off the lip so the rock edge and strata read clearly, and add a faint dashed descent path plus slight wind-lean on the figure to state 'safe descent' vs. 'danger.' 2) Make the cliff dramatic and the depth real — replace the flat brown wall with 4–6 distinct strata bands of varied tone, fracture lines, and a lit rim at the lip; add 3 receding landscape layers with a progressive haze/contrast falloff and 1–2 tiny scale references (far ridge, cloud wisp, bird) to sell altitude. 3) Upgrade the hero objects — give the canopy a wind-tilted, cell-structured shape with a leading-edge highlight and trailing shadow so it reads as a parachute; enlarge/contrast the figure into a clear suspended silhouette with a visible harness; make the taut lines crisp, converging, and slightly highlighted; reposition the sun so its halo no longer muddies the canopy rim. 4) Resolve the control trade-off — either wire WIND/DESCENT RATE/LIVE TELEMETRY to the SVG with a few lines of inline vanilla JS (streak speed, canopy tilt, altitude readout) so the telemetry is genuinely live, or restyle them as static instrument readouts (no slider affordance) and deduplicate the 4.6 value; keep the offline self-contained constraint. 5) Tidy the annotations — cut to at most three callouts, raise label size/contrast, route leaders through negative space (or move them to a side legend) so they never cross the canopy. 6) Final craft pass — remove the unresolved dark band at the scene's left edge, ensure the page bottom doesn't clip the NOMINAL status, and confirm header + scene compose as one legible single page.
